title: BUN/creatinine did not improve prediction of rested repeated-grip decrement across separate NHANES samples
abstract: In 3,749 NHANES 2011–2012 adults aged 20–79, we fitted weighted ridge models predicting bilateral first-to-third grip decrement from peak strength, demographics, body size and individual BUN and creatinine concentrations. Adding BUN/creatinine worsened source PSU-grouped cross-validation and changed MSE by +0.002829 percentage-points squared in 4,217 separately sampled 2013–2014 adults (95% rescaled target-PSU interval −0.000334 to +0.005926; source-and-target refit interval −0.712949 to +0.470518). Sensitivity analyses did not establish stable benefit. Trial-three strength generally exceeded trial-one strength. These rested contractions therefore cannot be assumed to measure clinical fatigability. The result does not support extending the ratio as a catabolism-linked predictor of this repeated-grip phenotype, but cannot rule out effects in clinical fatigue challenges.
